slides.title: Housekeeping and energy can fund the board's margin target
slides.subtitle: Alder & Vale Hotels · diagnostic for the COO
slides.notes: Fictional company and data. Built from samples/source/alder-vale-hotels/input via scripts/ingest.py. Data decision: the COO email gives rooms revenue as about $240M [F0002]; the FY25 summary gives $233M [F0009]. The deck uses the summary, the system figure.

slides.title: Matching the peer median on housekeeping and energy adds 2.2 pts of EBITDA margin
slides.answer: The two gaps are worth $5.0M a year and lift EBITDA margin from 15.8% to 18.0%, without cutting the service standard guests notice.

points.lead: Housekeeping costs 13.9% of rooms revenue, above the 12.9% peer median: $2.4M a year.
dashes: Every room gets a full clean daily, even on one-night stays.

points.lead: Energy costs $39.9 per room-night sold, above the $34.9 median: $2.6M a year.
dashes: Guest-room HVAC runs whether or not the room is sold.
Only 3 of 10 hotels have occupancy-linked thermostats.

points.lead: Together the gaps add 2.2 points, more than the 2 the board asked for.
dashes: The surplus gives room to protect service scores.

points.lead: Start with a light-refresh standard for short stays and thermostat retrofits.
dashes: Each acts on the largest driver of its gap.

slides.notes: Rooms revenue $233M [F0009]; housekeeping $32.4M [F0010]; energy $20.8M [F0011]; EBITDA $36.8M [F0013]; peer medians [F0071, F0072]. calc: housekeeping 13.9% = 32.4 / 232.6 [F0010, F0009]. calc: gap $2.4M = 32.4 - 12.9% x 232.6 [F0071]. calc: energy $39.9 per room-night = 20.8M / 521,500 room-nights (sum of hotel rows) [F0011, F0008-F0064]. calc: gap $2.6M = (39.9 - 34.9) x 521,500 [F0072]. calc: $5.0M = 2.4 + 2.6. calc: 15.8% = 36.8 / 232.6; 18.0% = (36.8 + 5.0) / 232.6; 2.2 pts = 18.0 - 15.8 [F0009]. calc: Airport 15.9% from the hotel rows [F0008-F0064]. Board ask 2 points [F0001]. Thermostats 3 of 10 [F0005, F0006, F0008].

slides.notes: calc: segment $/room-night = sum(energy_k) x 1000 / sum(room_nights): City 33.3, Airport 34.5, Resort 71.9 [F0008-F0064]. calc: energy $39.9 per room-night = 20.8M / 521,500 room-nights (sum of hotel rows) [F0011, F0008-F0064]. calc: gap $2.6M = (39.9 - 34.9) x 521,500 [F0072]. calc: 5.0 = 39.9 - 34.9 [F0072]. 30% [F0004].

slides.title: Closing both gaps lifts hotel EBITDA from $36.8M to $41.8M
slides.source: Alder & Vale FY25 hotel P&L; peer benchmarks

slides.title: Three levers act on how rooms are cleaned, cooled, and scheduled; two come first

points.text: Clean one-night rooms to a refresh standard (bed, bathroom, bins) and keep the full clean for stays of two nights or more.
Set unsold rooms to a set-back temperature. Only 3 of 10 hotels have the controls; a retrofit costs about $1,100 per room.
Plan housekeeping hours from forecast departures, not from a fixed daily roster.

slides.takeaway: The first two levers leave what guests notice unchanged.
slides.source: General manager and engineering interviews, July 2026
slides.notes: Interview facts: short-stay standard [F0005]; thermostats 3 of 10 and $1,100 per room [F0005, F0007].
